classification.class: invalid free while unwinding XInclude fallback node copying

bug_description.original: Invalid free and uninitialized-value in XInclude processing: while processing XInclude nodes (xmlXIncludeDoProcess in xinclude.c), libxml2's node-copy/free path (xmlStaticCopyNode/xmlFreeNode/xmlFreeNodeList/xmlFreeDoc in tree.c) attempts to free a pointer that was not returned by malloc (free on an interior address of an allocated block), causing heap corruption and crashes. MSAN also reports a use-of-uninitialized-value in the same XInclude/doc node creation path (xmlDictLookup/xmlNewDocNode), leading to undefined behavior and further memory corruption risk.
bug_description.normalized: The staged ASan trace closes on XInclude fallback copying. The PoC bytes are first consumed by xmlReadMemory in the fuzz/xml target, then XInclude processing walks an xi:include, the include load fails, and xmlXIncludeLoadFallback copies fallback children with xmlDocCopyNodeList. While xmlStaticCopyNode is recursively building that replacement subtree, a descendant copy fails and the function unwinds through xmlFreeNode and xmlFreeNodeList. During cleanup, xmlFreeNodeList reaches DICT_FREE(cur->name) on a node name pointer that ASan reports is 87 bytes inside a dictionary allocation from xmlDictAddString/xmlDictLookup, producing the witnessed invalid free on an interior address. The saved MSAN run is only partially symbolized, so this GT anchors to the fully source-grounded bad-free chain that is explicitly supported by the staged vulnerable source and the authoritative ASan stack.

source.code: doc = xmlReadMemory(docBuffer, docSize, docUrl, NULL, opts);
source.value_from: PoC-controlled main XML entity bytes and option word consumed by the fuzz/xml target.
source.description: This is the first project statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the attacker-controlled main XML bytes and materializes the document later sent into XInclude processing.

sink.description: Recursive cleanup frees a copied node name pointer as though it were a standalone allocation, but the saved ASan trace shows the pointer is an interior address inside a dictionary string pool.

root_cause.description: After include loading fails, fallback handling copies fallback children into the include replacement list. The saved crash stack shows this copy descending into xmlStaticCopyNodeList/xmlStaticCopyNode and then unwinding through the invalid-free cleanup path.

parser_admitted.code: doc = xmlReadMemory(docBuffer, docSize, docUrl, NULL, opts);
parser_admitted.description: The witness bytes are accepted by the XML parser and materialized as an xmlDoc before the XInclude-specific path is evaluated.

tainted_value_origin.code: doc = xmlReadMemory(docBuffer, docSize, docUrl, NULL, opts);
tainted_value_origin.description: The main PoC XML bytes and the option word controlling XInclude are first consumed together when the fuzz/xml target parses the in-memory document.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz/xml target reads an option word from the PoC and parses the main XML entity with xmlReadMemory.
With XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE enabled, XInclude traversal finds an xi:include node and schedules loading of its replacement content.
The include load fails, so xmlXIncludeLoadNode walks the xi:include children and dispatches the xi:fallback branch.
Fallback loading copies the fallback children into the include-table replacement subtree via xmlDocCopyNodeList.
A descendant copy fails, xmlStaticCopyNode frees the partially built copy, and recursive cleanup reaches DICT_FREE(cur->name) on the bad interior pointer observed by ASan.

fine_trace.note: The fuzz/xml target consumes the first PoC word as parser options. Reaching the vulnerable path requires this value to keep XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE enabled.

fine_trace.code: doc = xmlReadMemory(docBuffer, docSize, docUrl, NULL, opts);
fine_trace.note: The attacker-controlled main XML entity bytes are parsed into an xmlDoc using the PoC-selected parser flags, creating the document tree later traversed by XInclude.
Only inputs whose option word sets the XInclude flag reach xmlXIncludeProcessFlags and the downstream xi:include handling logic.

When the referenced xi:include resource cannot be loaded, xmlXIncludeLoadNode iterates the include element's children, finds xi:fallback, and dispatches fallback loading instead of abandoning the include site.

Fallback handling copies the fallback child list into a replacement subtree for the failed include. The authoritative ASan stack shows this exact call entering xmlStaticCopyNodeList and xmlStaticCopyNode on the crashing path.

depends_on.via: ret < 0 include-load failure with xi:fallback present

fine_trace.note: Recursive subtree copying asks for a copy of the next descendant from the fallback subtree and appends each successful child into the partially built destination tree.

If a descendant copy returns NULL, xmlStaticCopyNode immediately unwinds by freeing the partially built destination node `ret`. The ASan stack places this cleanup call directly above xmlFreeNode and xmlFreeNodeList on the crashing path.

Recursive cleanup descends into the copied subtree and frees a node name pointer as though it were a separately allocated string. The saved ASan report shows the freed address is 87 bytes inside a 1048-byte dictionary allocation created by xmlDictAddString/xmlDictLookup, so this DICT_FREE becomes the witnessed bad free on an interior address.

sanitizer_ground_truth.trace_format: saved ASan default crash trace plus partially symbolized MSAN reproduction trace

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The staged fix gates XPointer location-set support behind LIBXML_XPTR_LOCS_ENABLED, removing the XInclude/XPointer behaviors implicated by this sample. The saved vulnerable ASan stack itself closes on xmlXIncludeLoadFallback -> xmlDocCopyNodeList -> xmlStaticCopyNode -> xmlFreeNodeList, so the source-grounded root cause remains the witnessed fallback-copy entry into that unwinding chain rather than the allocation site in dict.c.

format.name: libxml2 fuzz/xml corpus input
format.contract: A single witness begins with the 4-byte option word consumed by `xmlFuzzReadInt`, followed by the fuzz-string/entity encoding consumed by `xmlFuzzReadEntities`. The verified trigger semantics require that this input make `xmlReadMemory` accept the main XML entity, set `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE`, and reach an `xi:include` failure path that uses an `xi:fallback` child so `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback` invokes `xmlDocCopyNodeList` on fallback children.
